stages: I found the buyer, order value and commercial terms. Let’s check them before you confirm.
The order says Net 30, but your quote says Net 15. The buyer check is still open. Let’s resolve both.
I’ve prepared a clarification and a verification request. Review them before anything is sent.
In this sample, the deal is complete. Its documents and decisions are ready for the next transaction.
flows: Start with an email, a PDF, a spreadsheet or a conversation. TRAIBOX is designed to capture the details, compare the terms and show you what still needs checking.
Resolve the gaps, bring in the right people and prepare the approved actions. Connect payment or funding requirements to the deal instead of starting a separate process.
Keep the documents, decisions and outcomes together. Reuse relevant, current information on the next deal and spend less time repeating the same work.
uses: See your opportunities, orders and open actions together. Know what is ready, what is waiting and who needs to act.
A single view of the deal, from first intent to final record.
Turn messy inputs into a clear plan.
Capture an email, upload a PDF or describe a deal. Agents help interpret documents, spot gaps and prepare the next steps.
See the evidence behind the proposed action.
Know who you are doing business with.
Organize buyers, suppliers and partners. Bring relevant company information and reusable evidence into each deal.
Connect once; reuse current information when permitted.
Connect the deal to the money.
Bring payment terms, funding needs and settlement into the same workflow. Compare relevant options through financial providers.
Prepare a finance-ready evidence package; provider approval is separate.
Know what needs to be cleared.
Review identity, relevant requirements, supporting documents and unresolved checks. Keep the reasons and evidence together.
Keep decisions traceable. No guarantee of compliance.
layers: An order tells a story: who is buying, what they want, when they need it and what both sides have agreed. Give people and agents that same starting point.
A coherent representation of the deal that people and agents can work from.
Find the gaps before they cost you.
Compare the order with the quote and the relevant rules. Show what matches, what does not and what still needs checking.
An explainable view of what is ready and what still needs attention.
Turn a finding into a next step.
Prepare the clarification, assign the work and ask the right person to approve it. A finding should lead somewhere useful.
Controlled progress, not autonomous commitments without authority.
Keep the documents, decisions and outcomes that matter. Next time, check what is still valid and who is allowed to use it.
Business-specific knowledge that can accumulate over time.
Work with what you already use.
Your ERP still holds the records. Your bank still handles the money. TRAIBOX is designed to coordinate the work between supported tools and providers.
Interoperability with existing systems, subject to supported integrations.

story.title: The order arrives.
story.copy: A buyer sends a purchase order. TRAIBOX brings the important details into one working record.

story.title: Something doesn’t match.
story.copy: The quote says Net 15; the order says Net 30. The agent flags the difference and identifies a pending buyer check.
story.note: Two items need attention before confirmation.

story.title: Prepare the work.
story.copy: Draft a clarification to the buyer and prepare a verification request. The commercial team reviews the proposed actions.
story.note: Nothing is sent without approval in this example.

story.title: Your team makes the call.
story.copy: The commercial lead reviews the evidence and proposed clarification. Choose whether to approve the simulated action or hold it.
story.note: This is a simulated approval. No real message is sent.

story.title: From agreement to payment.
story.copy: Assume the buyer accepted Net 15, verification was completed, and delivery and payment were confirmed by the relevant providers. TRAIBOX records those events.
story.note: No funds moved. Provider events are fictional.

story.title: The next deal starts ahead.
story.copy: Keep the agreed terms, supporting records and decisions together. When the buyer returns, check the information is still valid and reuse what is permitted.
story.note: Knowledge stays within the authorized business context.

texts: Bring the order, quotation and company details into a shared transaction context.
Coordinate checks, decisions and approved requests across your existing systems and partners.
Keep the useful records and decisions connected to the next deal.
stack: Bring relevant commercial information from your existing systems into a transaction review, and return authorized updates where supported.
Capture relevant marketplace orders and associated commercial details into the deal context.
Use relevant shipment and delivery events to update the transaction, without replacing logistics providers.
Prepare requests and receive status updates through supported financial providers, subject to approval.
Request appropriate checks through providers and preserve relevant results with the deal.
